# SPE round 3 plan

Round 3 tests one fix per config against the round 2 baseline. C gets the outage status check back as its own tool. D gets a retry cap. A and B stay unchanged as controls. Every cell runs 5 trials. A new slice of 10 hard tickets is scored on its own, so the original ticket set stays comparable to round 2.

The naive guess ("same as last round") beat my round 2 predictions in 4 of 5 rows. The other row was a tie. This round I start from the round 2 numbers and move a number only when a known mechanism explains the move.

## Specify

### Decisions on the round 2 proposals

| ID | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Adopt | F4 names a specific mechanism. The merged tool hid the outage status check, so outage tickets got P3. |
| P2 | Adopt, with a change | Category accuracy of 0.86 is not at ceiling, but mixed tickets do test a weakness we have not measured. If I mixed the hard tickets into the main set, the main metric would no longer compare to round 2. So the 10 tickets become a separate "hard" slice with their own numbers. |
| P3 | Reject for now | D gives the only cost row. Dropping D would end the cost signal. F6 has a known cause, so I cap retries in D and measure again. Logged as default D1. |
| P4 | Adopt | B's miss (0.88 predicted, 0.86 measured) falls inside noise at n=3. Five trials per cell narrows that. |

### Requirements (round 3 table for `spe/spec/spec.md`)

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R3-1 | Config C calls the outage status check as a separate tool. The rest of C's tool merge stays as it was. | r02 F4, P1 | In the dry run on T17, C calls the status check and returns the oracle priority. In the full run, the status check shows up in C transcripts for outage tickets. |
| R3-2 | Add 10 hard tickets that mix billing and outage issues. Score them as slice `hard`, apart from the original set. | P2 | The results table reports the original set and `hard` in separate rows. |
| R3-3 | Config D allows at most 1 Haiku retry per ticket. This is D's only change. | r02 F6, P3 rejected | No D trial logs more than 1 retry. |
| R3-4 | Run 5 trials per cell. | P4 | Trial count per cell is 5, plus logged extra trials for split cells. |
| R3-5 | The grader reads priority from `label.priority` and never from the draft reply. | r02 F5 | A selftest case has "P1" in the draft reply and P3 in `label.priority`. The grader must score it as P3. |
| R3-6 | `spe/prediction-log.md` shows the original r02 numbers next to the regraded ones. | r02 F5, close-out rule | The r02 section has an "Original (pre-F5)" column. |
| R3-7 | Configs A and B stay unchanged from round 2. | Control | The config diff for A and B against r02 is empty. |

### Defaults logged in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`

- **D1.** I keep D with a retry cap instead of dropping it. If you would rather drop D, say "drop D" and I will remove D's rows before saving the prediction.
- **D2.** Labeling rule for mixed tickets: when the service is down, the category is outage. Otherwise the category is billing. I write the oracle labels before the run and commit them with the harness.
- **D3.** The excerpt does not give the size of the original ticket set. I assume 20 tickets for the cost estimate. I will correct this from the r02 eval files before launch.

## Predict

The hit rule is the same as in round 2. A cell marked "r02" takes the exact round 2 measured value from the r02 results. The draft YAML only carried category baselines, so I will copy those r02 values into `r03.yaml` before the run without moving them.

### Original ticket set

| Metric | A | B | C | D | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | 0.86 | 0.86 | 0.82 | 0.74 | `grade.py`: exact match of `label.category` against the oracle |
| priority accuracy | r02 | r02 | 0.77 | r02 | `grade.py`: exact match of `label.priority` against the oracle (F5 fix) |
| cost per ticket | r02 | r02 | r02 | $0.003 | Mean of API usage tokens times the price table, per ticket |

**Why, per row:**
- **Category accuracy.** A and B have no change, so they stay at 0.86. C moves from 0.80 to 0.82 because it gets one of its merged tools back. The rest of the merge stays, so I expect only a partial return toward the round 1 value of 0.84. D's retry cap should not change which category Haiku picks, so D stays at 0.74.
- **Priority accuracy.** C moves from 0.71 to 0.77. I assume most of the drop from 0.78 to 0.71 came from outage tickets that got P3 (F4). Restoring the status check should recover most of that. The other configs have no change that touches priority.
- **Cost per ticket.** D moves from $0.004 to $0.003. F6 found that retries doubled tokens on long tickets, and the cap removes most of those extra calls. The other configs have no change that affects tokens in a way I can size.

### Hard slice (new, no round 2 baseline)

| Metric | A | B | C | D | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy (hard) | 0.70 | 0.70 | 0.66 | 0.58 | `grade.py` on tickets tagged `slice: hard`, scored against the D2 labels |

**Why:** A mixed ticket has two plausible categories. I expect A and B to miss about 3 of 10. For C and D, I subtract each config's predicted gap to A on the original set. Priority on the hard slice is measured as a diagnostic, but it is not a scored prediction this round.

## Evaluate

The harness is `spe/evals/harness/r03-workflow.js`. It holds the round in one constant, `ROUND = 3`. Prompt text gets the round from that constant.

### Steps and gates

1. **Write the hard tickets.** Put the 10 tickets in the ticket set. Put their oracle labels in the grader-only directory, where trials cannot read them.
2. **Grader selftest.** The oracle must pass. An empty answer must fail. A wrong answer must fail. The F5 case from R3-5 must score P3. *Gate:* if any check fails, halt.
3. **Control regrade.** Run the current `grade.py` on the r02 transcripts. It must reproduce the regraded r02 numbers: category A 0.86, B 0.86, C 0.80, and priority C 0.71. *Gate:* if any number differs, halt and report a broken grader.
4. **Dry run on 3 cells.**
   - C on T17. C must call the status check and give the oracle priority.
   - D on the longest ticket. D must log 1 retry or fewer.
   - A on one hard ticket. The output must pass the schema, and the grader must read it.

   *Gate:* all 3 must pass.
5. **Full run.** 4 configs, (20 + 10) tickets, 5 trials each, for 600 trials.
6. **Peek scan.** Scan every transcript for reads of the grader, the oracle labels, or `spe/predictions/`. Void any trial that peeked, and log it.
7. **Split cells.** A cell is split when its trials disagree on the same ticket. Each split cell gets up to 3 extra trials. Total extra trials are capped at 60.
8. **Failure analysis.** Check whether F4 and F6 are fixed. Name any new failure types for `failures.md`.
9. **Completeness critic.** Confirm that every predicted cell has a measured value and that every skip and void is logged.

### Trial schema

`{ticket_id, slice, label: {category, priority}, draft_reply, tool_calls[], retries, usage: {input_tokens, output_tokens}}`

Code checks score category, priority, retries, and tool calls. No judge is needed this round.

### Workflow arguments

```
ROUND: 3
configs: [A, B, C, D]
ticket_sets: [original, hard]
trials_per_cell: 5
split_extra_trials_per_cell: 3
split_extra_trials_total_cap: 60
budget_cap_usd: 25
on_cap: skip remaining trials and log each skip
```

### Cost estimate (unmeasured)

D runs 150 trials at about $0.003, which is about $0.45. For A, B, and C, I assume about $0.02 per ticket. That gives 450 trials for about $9. Extra trials, failure analysis, and the critic add about $3 to $5. My total estimate is about $13 to $15. The hard cap is $25.

## After approval

1. Save the pasted text and "ok, next one" verbatim to `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r03.md`.
2. Add the round 3 table to `spe/spec/spec.md` and mark P1 to P4 as decided. Add D1 to D3 to `disagreements.md`. Add the original r02 numbers to the prediction log (R3-6). Commit `SPE r03 specify: adopt P1 P2 P4, replace P3 with D retry cap`.
3. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r03.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r03.yaml` and start it with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It records round 3, date 2026-10-21, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", the configs, every number with its Why, and `same_as_last_round`. I leave `r03-draft.yaml` as it is. Commit `SPE r03 predict: C split outage tool, D retry cap, n=5`.
4. Build the harness and run gates 2 to 4. Commit `SPE r03 evaluate (harness): ...`.
5. Launch the Workflow. It returns at launch. When the completion notice arrives, commit `SPE r03 evaluate (results): <headline>`.
6. Close out the round. Update the prediction log, failures, the round 4 proposals, the r04 draft, and the README. Commit `SPE r03 learn: ...` and tag `spe-r03`.

All commits stay local. I will not push.

**Halt and report if** the budget cap is hit, an answer key leaks, the grader fails a gate, or a decision comes up that only you can make.

The "Decisions on the round 2 proposals" table covers every proposal. P1 is adopted because of F4. P2 is adopted with a change, as a separate hard slice. P3 is rejected for now because D carries the only cost signal. P4 is adopted because of noise at n=3. Each decision has a reason.

The "Why, per row" bullets explain each moved number. C category moves to 0.82 because one tool comes back as a partial fix. C priority moves to 0.77 because of the F4 recovery.
